result: The ExA-SPIM system combines metrology optics with tissue expansion to achieve large field of view (13.3 mm diameter), long working distance (35 mm), moderate NA (0.305), effective resolution of ~0.5 µm laterally and ~1 µm axially with 3× expansion, and high imaging speed (946 megavoxels/s). The system can image >100 teravoxels with minimal tiling and no sectioning.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm the technical specifications and capabilities of ExA-SPIM. Reviewer 1 states the methodology is 'characterized and supported by convincing evidence' and provides 'an impressive field of view.' Reviewer 2 describes 'an exceptional combination of field of view, working distance, resolution and throughput' and notes that 'an expanded mouse brain can be acquired with only 15 tiles.' Reviewer 3 confirms 'the microscope design and characterization is a useful contribution to the field.'

result: A novel expansion microscopy protocol was developed for centimeter-scale tissue samples including entire mouse brains, using stringent dehydration and delipidation (THF followed by DISCO-type clearing and aqueous delipidation), VA-044 initiator for gelation, and temperature-controlled polymerization to achieve nearly isotropic expansion.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the expansion protocol as part of the overall ExA-SPIM methodology. Reviewer 1 states the 'ExA-SPIM methodology developed here' is 'supported by convincing evidence.' Reviewer 2 notes 'the authors also present an expansion method optimized for whole mouse brains' as part of the impressive work. No concerns are raised about the expansion protocol itself.

result: ExA-SPIM enables imaging of sparsely labeled neurons in expanded mouse brains (3×) in 15 tiles in as little as 24 hours, with alignment accuracy <2 pixels between tiles. Dense axonal projections, varicosities, and long-range axons are clearly visible, and the resulting image volumes are sufficient for manual neuron tracing.
evaluation: Reviewers affirm the imaging quality and neuron tracing capabilities. Reviewer 2 states 'the image data is compelling, and tracing of neurons has been performed. This demonstrates the potential of the microscope platform.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the data are quite stunning' and acknowledges that while 'the manuscript would be stronger if the authors had been able to provide data that justified the original high-impact claims...for robust and automated neuronal tracing,' the 'amended manuscript text now more closely matches the supporting data,' indicating acceptance of the manual tracing claims.

result: ExA-SPIM was successfully applied to image a 1 cm³ block of pigtail macaque motor cortex (a heavily myelinated region difficult to clear), revealing brightly labeled cortico-spinal neurons with clearly discernible dendritic arbors, spines, descending axons, and collaterals. Axonal pathways can be followed even in down-sampled data.
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about the macaque brain imaging results. Reviewer 2 describes the overall work as 'impressive' and representing 'a leap over existing light-sheet microscopes,' which encompasses the macaque imaging demonstrations. Reviewer 3 states 'the data are quite stunning,' referring to all example images including the macaque data. The lack of specific critique indicates acceptance of these findings.

result: ExA-SPIM imaging of 4× expanded human neocortex sections (~100 µm thick) revealed individual axons and their trajectories with high contrast. Larger axons (>1 µm) are well separated in both gray and white matter, and white matter axons are arranged as multiple intercalated populations coursing in different directions rather than homogeneous fascicles.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the human brain imaging results as part of the overall demonstration. Reviewer 2 notes 'the microscope is employed in imaging an expanded mouse brain, the macaque motor cortex and human brain slices of white matter' as part of the impressive work. Reviewer 3 confirms the authors 'show example images of expanded samples from mouse, macaque, and human brain tissue' and states 'the data are quite stunning.' No specific concerns are raised about the human tissue results.

result: Preliminary data suggests that automated segmentation of thin axons is improved with ExA-SPIM compared to previous approaches.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly addresses this claim, noting 'the manuscript would be stronger if the authors had been able to provide data that justified the original high-impact claims from the initial publication (e.g. that the images could be used for robust and automated neuronal tracing across large volumes).' This indicates the reviewer found the evidence for automated tracing insufficient, though they accept that 'the amended manuscript text now more closely matches the supporting data,' suggesting the claim has been appropriately qualified as preliminary.

result: The large field of view of ExA-SPIM permits imaging cleared mouse brains in a single tile, with datasets acquired at ~1.5 µm lateral resolution in ~36 min/channel.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the cleared tissue imaging capabilities. Reviewer 2 notes the system is 'designed to image expanded mouse brains in their entirety' and can image 'the entire expanded mouse brain at cellular and subcellular resolution' (Reviewer 1). The ability to image cleared brains is presented as an additional application and is not questioned by reviewers.

result: Custom acquisition software was developed for ExA-SPIM that interfaces with the VP-151MX camera driver and streams data to next-generation file formats, enabling throughput to cloud storage of >100 TB per day using commodity hardware.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly notes 'the authors also present...an acquisition software suite' as part of the impressive work. No concerns are raised about the software or data handling capabilities, indicating acceptance of these technical developments.

result: Photobleaching is not detrimental at the imaging conditions used by ExA-SPIM (~50% reduction in intensity after ~800 repeated exposures).
evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about photobleaching or the high laser powers used. The overall acceptance of the imaging quality and technical characterization by all reviewers implicitly supports this finding.

result: ExA-SPIM's approach of combining lower NA optics (0.305) with tissue expansion provides advantages including: more forgiving optical engineering requirements, larger fields of view and working distances, easier correction of optical distortions, reduced sensitivity to tissue-induced aberrations, and favorable scaling of aberrations with expansion factor.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the conceptual and technical novelty of the approach. Reviewer 3 states 'the primary conceptual and technical novelty is to use a detection objective from the metrology industry that has a large field of view and a large area camera,' acknowledging the optical design strategy. The overall positive assessment of the system's performance by all reviewers supports the claimed advantages of this approach.
